doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Ernest's violin lessons and banjo
summary: He started violin lessons in 1910, later got a banjo, and recalls early pieces.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: And when did you get interested in music?

Oh, me, I had started in 1910, but I never exactly completed. I gave it up when I seen it wasn't using violin so much, I just put it down. I played a line there a little, you know, just for home, but I never did finish. Here on, I had to finish line for nothing. It came out to me. I was doing pretty good. I had a good start. Yeah, I took my first lesson in 1910. It was the great day present my grandmother that started. Yeah.
How long did you take?
Oh, I went with him about a year and a half. I think I still have my book home. First book I studied.
I'd like to see it.
I think I still have it. I'm going to see if I'm okay.
He keeps all those things, you know.
If I don't have it, my oldest daughter's got it.
Hmm? You keep a few years. Oh, yeah, the D.
He keeps it. Yeah, he tried to entice me to finish by all means. I'm sorry I didn't.
I'm sorry I didn't finish. Did you take a banjo later?

Well, under my forein-law, you know. He taught me some. Well, Frank knew a few chords. I didn't know a few chords. But the old man used to use the sword dog that much. Yeah, I got mad in the sword. He never would give me nothing. I bought it. I bought it. The fella had it in pawn and he sold me the ticket. I got it out for $34. It was $154. A big orduphonic banjo. It was beautiful.
Those Vegas are beautiful. Yeah, it was beautiful. It was beautiful. It was beautiful. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Did you play any other instruments?
I played a little mad one. Well, that's Sam Fing and his violin. He said he got double string on that one.
When you were young, what music do you remember? Music or singing? Very early.
Well, the first, one of the first pieces I learned to play on the violin. Can you sing them like Sister Kay? I never forget that song.
Yeah.
Yeah, Donnebue Waltz. I was in the house. All the old letters were in books, you know. I prepared a book about that wide and about that long.
You learned Sister Kay back in 19...
1910 or 1911. I started in 10.
He's telling me.

Yeah. That's where I started. In 10. That was in a book or you were just heard? Well, it was a piano copy. I think I bought it by Willow in the 90s. Willow on Knausley. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I heard that. Yes, years ago. I never forget that song. I think about it, you know. Just like that. stuff one of those clubs, I just remember the name of it. Yeah, he had a band running then. The Elkish. Tuxley Elkish.
